text:
Amanda L.: Heads up — customer X is asking for a safer rollback path for tenant network changes in the private deploy (VPC + on-prem). They want a staged ship + quick patchback option. Thoughts?

Raj P.: +1 we should define a 3-step rollout: canary (1 tenant), ramp (10%), broad. each step with automatic rollback on health check failures.

Maria S.: @Raj P. customer just called: their netops insists on deterministic IP persistence during upgrade. if we replace connectors we need a preserved IP plan or a NAT handoff.

Raj P.: noted. proposal: 1) preserve overlay subnets where possible, 2) if connector IPs change, do a short-lived NAT mapping for 48h, 3) advertise graceful deprecation to customer.

Dylan T.: we can implement NAT handoff via the agent: attach a `static-nat` mode in installer. sample config snippet:```yaml
agent:
  network:
    mode: static-nat
    nat_window: 48h
    preserve_routes: true
```

FieldOps Bot: Ticket created: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/PD-9745 — "tenant-network-patchback-plan". Linked ops doc: https://docs.internal/redwood/private-deploy/patchback-guidance

sre-bot: Deploy policy check: canary -> ramp requires health probes on /_status (200 for 5m) + p50 latency < 200ms. Auto-rollback hook available via `redwood-agent rollback --tenant $TENANT`.

Amanda L.: Important ask from field: minimal downtime during upgrade (<=2min per tenant). Can the NAT approach meet that?

Dylan T.: yes if we do in-place connector restart with preserved MAC/IP and warm KV cache. Worst-case with NAT it's <2m if flows are re-proxied quickly. But we need to script flow: `kubectl rollout restart daemonset/redwood-agent -n onprem` + iptables sync.

Maria S.: Edge case: air-gapped customers can't accept external NAT controllers. For them we need an 'offline patchback' artifact that installs the nat mappings locally.

Raj P.: plan for air-gapped: produce a small offline tool `patchback-apply.tar.gz` that netops runs. It applies iptables rules and a local mapping daemon. Document deliverable in the launch checklist.

Amanda L.: Let's align on launch criteria for this feature set: 1) documented rollback runbook, 2) automated canary + healthchecks, 3) patchback artifact for offline installs, 4) field-tested on 2 customers, 5) telemetry showing no more than 2 incidents in internal rollout.

Dylan T.: I'll own: automated rollout + rollback scripts and canary gating (ETA 2 wks).

Maria S.: I'll own: field validation, create runbook and offline patchback package, coordinate with customer X next Wed.

Raj P.: I'll own: release policy and network-preservation design (including NAT timeout default = 48h).

Amanda L.: Risks: IP overlap between tenants during NAT window, customer firewall rules that block ephemeral IPs. Add mitigation: preflight check that fails rollout if overlap detected.

sre-bot: Preflight note: implement `net-preflight --tenant $TENANT` which checks CIDR overlap, firewall reachability, and required ports (22, 443, 80, 9000).

FieldOps Bot: FYI — Customer X field engineer @leo requested the offline tool to support RHEL7. tagging @Maria S.

Maria S.: Acked. I'll include RHEL7 in the compatibility matrix.

Amanda L.: Action items summary: Dylan -> rollout scripts, Raj -> design + policy, Maria -> runbook + offline package + field test. Owners to post progress in this thread by EOD Friday.

Raj P.: one more q: do we need to expose an admin UI toggle to trigger patchback/preserve mode, or is CLI enough?

Amanda L.: prefer CLI for v1, admin UI toggle for v2 (unless field demands UI now).

Dylan T.: CLI + operator annotation should be fine: `kubectl annotate tenant/ACME redwood.io/patchback=enabled`

Maria S.: I'll surface the UI ask in customer call; if they push we'll prioritize.

Amanda L.: Cool. thanks everyone. leaving notes in PD-9745. :white_check_mark:
